title: Standardizing Regional Logistics Reporting
business: A global logistics firm managing disparate regional supply chain databases.
problem: The firm suffers from inconsistent reporting logic where regional analysts define 'transit time' differently, leading to conflicting executive dashboards and high maintenance overhead for manual SQL scripts.
solution: The firm adopts dbt to implement a modular, SQL-first transformation workflow. By centralizing logic into version-controlled models, the team enforces a single source of truth for metrics, ensuring that every regional dashboard consumes the same underlying transformation logic.
steps: Define raw source tables using dbt source configurations to map regional database schemas.
Create staging models to perform initial data cleaning and column renaming for consistency.
Develop intermediate models to join regional transit data and apply standardized business logic.
Define final mart models that aggregate data for specific executive reporting requirements.
Utilize dbt state-aware orchestration to ensure only modified models are rebuilt during daily refreshes.
outcome: Improved data consistency across regional teams and reduced time spent debugging conflicting reports, as logic is now centralized and auditable.
limitation: A significant tradeoff is the complexity of managing dependency graphs as the project scales; developers must monitor the lineage to avoid circular references, which can be checked by reviewing the generated DAG in the dbt Catalog.
